title: Normalization of centered towers and regular pullback
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ be an ordinary blowup tower with coherent centers $I_i$ having nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Put $Y_0=X$, $Y_i=X_i^\nu$ for $i\geq1$ and $K_i=I_i\mathcal O_{Y_i}$, where for $i=0$ the structure map is the identity and $\nu$ denotes componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. These data form a normalized blowup tower with
$$Y_{i+1}\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{K_i}(Y_i)^\nu.$$
Its centers are coherent with nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes; if $X_n$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] then $Y_n=X_n$ canonically. A length-zero tower with regular input stays unchanged.

For a regular morphism $h:T\to S$ between reduced Noetherian schemes, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres, normalization commutes with base change:
$$T^\nu\simeq S^\nu\times_S T.$$
Consequently every finite normalized blowup tower on $S$ whose intermediate schemes are Noetherian has a scheme-theoretic recursive pullback to $T$; its centers are the extended ideals. These identifications respect identities and composition. For an ordinary tower as in the first paragraph, normalizing its regular pullback agrees with pulling back its normalized tower. Deleting a unit-center stage whose normalized blowup is an isomorphism commutes with these identifications; a nonidentity normalization at a unit-center stage is retained. Noetherian schemes here admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings. Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; extended ideals are [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and coherent means [pqf-def-coherent]. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]; regular morphisms mean flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism] with geometrically regular fibres, with the regular-ring-map convention of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: VIII Proposition 2.2.4(ii), 2.2.6, Lemma 2.2.9, Remark 2.3.3(i) and Remark 2.3.12(i), printed pp.90--94 No Stacks tag states this combined result; the cited place is in the archived ILO volume.

proof.text: First check finiteness in the ordinary-tower paragraph. Ordinary blowups are proper, hence finite type, so the finite-type stability of quasi-excellence keeps every $X_i$ quasi-excellent and Noetherian. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X_i$, quasi-excellence implies Nagata. Each $A/\mathfrak p$ for a minimal prime is therefore Japanese; taking its own fraction field in the N-2 definition shows that its integral closure is a finite module. The affine normalization formula is the finite product of these closures, so normalization is finite. Its coordinate rings are finite-type over $A$, hence Noetherian; finite affine covers give quasi-compactness. Thus all $Y_i$ are Noetherian, and extended finite-type quasi-coherent ideals are coherent by the cited coherence criterion.

source.place: VIII 2.2.1, 2.2.6 and Remark 2.3.3(i), pp.90--91; Stacks 07QU, 07QV (via cited nodes)

proof.text:
For one ordinary step $W=\operatorname{Bl}_J S$, let $N=W^
u$. The component-dominating normalization lift gives $N	o S^
u$. Compare $N$ and $M=(\operatorname{Bl}_{J\mathcal O_{S^
u}}S^
u)^
u$: both are normal, component-dominating, and principalize $J$. The normalization lift followed by normalized-blowup finality over $S^
u$ gives $N	o M$, and finality over $S$ gives $M	o N$. The composites are identities by uniqueness in finality. The extended center on $S^
u$ is nowhere dense because generic points correspond, and is coherent by Step 1, so both applications meet their hypotheses. For the first tower step use $Y_0=X$, with no initial normalization. For $i\ge1$ the displayed comparison applied to $S=X_i$ gives exactly $Y_{i+1}\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i\mathcal O_{Y_i}}(Y_i)^
u$. This constructs every stage and every connecting map by induction.

The zero scheme of $I_i\mathcal O_{Y_i}$ is the inverse image of $V(I_i)$. Surjectivity of normalization makes this nonempty; the generic-point bijection makes it nowhere dense. If $X_n$ is regular it is normal, so its normalization is canonically itself. For length zero the construction sets $Y_0=X$ and has no step; hence regular input is unchanged.

We give the normality argument without assuming finite normalization. On affine opens a regular map is $A\to R$ with both rings Noetherian. Popescu supplies $R=\varinjlim R_\lambda$ with smooth $A$-algebras. For any normal $A$-algebra $B$, each $B\otimes_A R_\lambda$ is smooth over $B$ by smooth base change, hence normal even when $B$ is not Noetherian. The tensor universal property identifies their filtered ring colimit with $B\otimes_A R$: maps out of either ring are precisely compatible pairs of maps out of $B$ and the $R_\lambda$ agreeing on $A$. Filtered colimits of normal rings are normal. Thus $B\otimes_A R$ is normal for every normal $B$, and the same argument applies after arbitrary base change of $A\to R$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 2.2.9, p.91, normality input expanded by Stacks 07GC, 033C and 037D

proof.text:
Write $B=\overline A\subseteq Q(A)$ for the affine normalization of a reduced Noetherian base and take $R$ from Step 4. That step makes $C=R\otimes_A B$ normal. The flat integral total-fraction lemma identifies $C$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$; the affine normalization formula therefore identifies $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $(\operatorname{Spec}R)^
u$. This is precisely $T^
u\simeq S^
u	imes_S T$ on the chosen opens. The formulas send $r\otimes b$ to $rQ(f)(b)$, so restriction to smaller affines gives the same map. They consequently glue to the canonical scheme comparison. This proves the assertion even for nonfinite normalization.

Now induct on the length of a normalized tower, keeping $Z_i=X_i\times_S T$ and the extended center. At stage zero $Z_0=T$. Ordinary blowup commutes with flat base change, with center ideals identified by its chartwise comparison. Apply the normalization calculation of Steps 4--5 to this square to obtain the next normalized stage. Here no unproved Noetherianity of $Z_i$ is needed: the projection to the original Noetherian $X_i$ is a base change of $h$, so its tensor algebras are filtered colimits of smooth algebras as in Step 4. Reducedness is also explicit: for an affine original stage with ring $D$, flat tensor exactness embeds its pullback ring $E$ into $E\otimes_D\overline D$, which is normal by Step 4, so $E$ is reduced. The source has locally finitely many components: by flat going-down its generic points lie over those of $X_i$; the generic fibres are the fibres of $T$ over the corresponding generic points of $S$, because each blowup and normalization preserves those generic fields. These fibres are localizations of Noetherian affine rings of $T$, with finitely many components. Blowup charts and integral intermediate total-fraction algebras preserve this generic description. Thus the affine normalization formula still applies. This completes the recursive pullback induction.

Identity and composite comparison maps agree on pure tensors: along $A\to R\to R'$, both send $r\otimes b$ to its image $r\,Q(A\to R')(b)$. On blowup charts both send $x/a$ to the corresponding extended fraction. The tensor and localization defining relations then give equality of the ring maps, and their compatible affine gluings give equality of scheme maps. Applying these equations successively at every stage proves identity and composition compatibility. Applying the same one-step equations to an ordinary tower, and inducting from its unchanged stage zero, identifies normalization after regular pullback with regular pullback after normalization, including the extended ideal centers.

For a unit center, the ordinary blowup is an isomorphism, so its normalized blowup is the normalization map. An isomorphism stage remains an isomorphism after pullback, since pulling back its inverse gives an inverse. Deleting that stage simply composes its adjacent arrows, and the composition equations of Step 7 identify both resulting towers with their remaining centers. If the normalization map is not an identity/isomorphism stage, retain it; the construction never deletes a stage merely because its ideal is the unit ideal. Finally choose the affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings supplied by local Noetherianity; quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover.
